rows.grounds: describes the mass as not divided by adding or taking away

items.question: What is meant by the term cosmic egg in this context?
premises: The mass turns toward manifestation.
It emerges from the form of power.
It is not divided by insertion or removal.
items.inference: Therefore this unified mass of reality is called the cosmic egg.
uncertainties: The exact nuance of āvāpa-vāpana in this cosmological context is slightly compressed.
items.plain_english: The cosmic egg is the mass of reality that has turned toward manifestation, emerged from the form of power, and remains undivided by any addition or removal.

rows.grounds: identifies the upper shell with sattva
identifies the lower part with sattva
names the lower covering's dominant quality

items.question: How are the upper and lower shells of the cosmic egg described?
premises: The upper shell is sattva touched by a trace of darkness.
The lower shell is sattva touched by activity.
The lower covering is associated with darkness.
items.inference: Thus the egg's two shells are differentiated by mixtures of the three qualities.
uncertainties: The syntax of nirmṛṣṭaṃ sattvam asyādharaṃ tamaḥ is compressed and allows slight interpretive variation.
items.plain_english: The upper shell of the egg is sattva mixed with a trace of darkness, while the lower shell is sattva mixed with activity and associated with darkness.

rows.grounds: introduces the reason for the name

items.question: Why is the mass of reality also called an egg?
premises: The mass of reality partakes of the collectivity of Shiva and Shakti.
In its manifestation there is a turning toward.
That turning toward explains the designation egg.
items.inference: Therefore the manifested mass of reality is called an egg because it turns toward manifestation as a unified Shiva-Shakti collectivity.
uncertainties: The compound śivaśaktisamūhabhāk could also be read more loosely as participating in their totality.
items.plain_english: The mass of reality is said to partake of the collectivity of Shiva and Shakti, and because it turns toward manifestation it is called an egg.

rows.grounds: explains why they are not eggs

items.question: Why do powers immersed in Shiva not become cosmic eggs?
premises: An objection arises that powers immersed in Shiva might also be eggs.
A further statement is given to address this objection.
Those powers have not fallen from the state of power.
items.inference: Therefore powers immersed in Shiva are not eggs because they have not undergone the fall into manifestation.
uncertainties: cyutaśaktitaḥ is compact; the reading 'fallen from the state of power' follows the argument but is interpretive.
items.plain_english: One might object that powers immersed in Shiva should also be eggs, but they are not, because they have not fallen from their own state of power.

items.question: Why should egg-ness not be extended to bodies and sense bases individually?
premises: A further word is added to prevent a wrong extension of egg-ness.
In bodies, sense bases, and so on, there is no insertion of anything.
Egg-ness depends on a condition not present there.
items.inference: Therefore egg-ness should not be wrongly applied to individual bodies and sense bases.
uncertainties: tanvakṣādi is a compact compound; 'body and sense basis and so on' is a contextual expansion.
items.plain_english: Another clarifying term is used so that egg-ness is not wrongly extended to bodies and sense bases, because nothing is inserted into them in that way.

rows.grounds: explains the function of the term

items.question: How can a collectivity of bodies and sense bases be one?
premises: A collectivity of bodies and sense bases raises the question of oneness.
The term undivided is used in response.
That term indicates sameness of kind.
items.inference: Therefore the collectivity is one because its members are undivided in kind.
uncertainties: sājātya may imply either sameness of kind or homogeneity; both fit the argument.
items.plain_english: If bodies and sense bases form a collectivity, their oneness is explained by the word 'undivided', which shows that they share the same kind.

items.question: Would egg-nature apply to each principle even without the term mass of reality?
premises: One might think each principle could be an egg even without the term mass of reality.
This would imply egg-nature in the principles individually.
The verse raises a challenge to that consequence.
items.inference: The text questions whether egg-nature can rightly be assigned to each principle on its own.
uncertainties: The verse is transitional and its force is partly completed by the next verse.
items.plain_english: Someone might think that, even without using the term 'mass of reality', each principle by itself could have the nature of an egg; but the text challenges that idea.

items.question: Why does egg-nature not improperly extend to a principle made of qualities, subtle elements, and gross elements?
premises: Egg-nature might seem to extend to a principle composed of qualities, subtle elements, and gross elements.
The answer appeals to the word reality.
Here reality means what consists of bodies, sense bases, and worlds.
items.inference: Therefore egg-nature does not extend improperly, because the relevant 'reality' is specifically the aggregate of bodies, sense bases, and worlds.
uncertainties: tanvakṣabhuvanātmakam compresses several levels; the translation keeps the standard doctrinal grouping.
items.plain_english: Egg-nature would wrongly extend to a principle made only of qualities, subtle elements, and gross elements; but the word 'reality' here means the whole made of bodies, sense bases, and worlds.

rows.grounds: grounds the collectivity in the Lord

items.question: On what basis is that collectivity called an egg?
premises: The relevant form has already been stated.
That form constitutes a collectivity.
Such collectivity belongs to the Lord who bears the universal body.
items.inference: Therefore that collectivity is called an egg because it is the unified form of the Lord's universal body.
uncertainties: The relation between collectivity and the Lord's body is doctrinally clear but syntactically compact.
items.plain_english: Because that form has already been defined, its collectivity is called an egg; and this collectivity belongs to the Lord who bears the universe as his body.

rows.grounds: names the domain where egg-ness is restricted

items.question: Why were additional distinguishing terms introduced in this explanation?
premises: Additional distinguishing terms were taken up for clarification.
The clarification concerns states limited to a certain extent.
Those states occur in the path-sphere dependent on Maya.
items.inference: Therefore the extra terms were introduced to prevent egg-ness from being misapplied outside the Maya-dependent path-sphere.
uncertainties: tāvanmātrāsu is general; the verse points to a restricted scope rather than naming it explicitly.
items.plain_english: For that reason, other distinguishing terms were introduced, to show that egg-ness applies only within the limited states of the path-sphere that depends on Maya.

rows.grounds: sets the boundary for what follows

items.question: What lies beyond the Brahma egg described so far?
premises: Some explain the distinguishing terms as preventing misapplied egg-ness.
Beyond the Brahma egg thus described there are Rudras.
Those Rudras number one hundred.
items.inference: Therefore, beyond the Brahma egg, the cosmology continues with a group of one hundred Rudras.
uncertainties: The shift from definitional discussion to enumeration is abrupt but clear.
items.plain_english: Others say the distinguishing terms were used to prevent egg-ness from being misapplied; in any case, beyond the Brahma egg described here there are one hundred Rudras.

items.question: Who are the lords ruling over the hundred Rudras?
premises: The hundred Rudras have their own lords.
Those lords are eleven Rudras of great radiance.
The verse begins listing their names.
items.inference: Therefore the hundred Rudras are governed by eleven radiant Rudra-lords, beginning with Ananta and others named here.
uncertainties: The compound kapālyāgniryamanairṛtakau packs several names; the segmentation follows standard lists but is slightly interpretive.
items.plain_english: Over those hundred Rudras stand eleven radiant Rudra-lords of their own: Ananta, Kapalin, Agni, Yama, Nairrita, Bala, and the rest named in sequence.

items.question: How is the surrounding presence of these Rudra-lords illustrated?
premises: The list of eleven Rudra-lords continues in this verse.
A simile compares them to bees around flowers.
Bees cover honey, kadamba clusters, and filament networks.
items.inference: Therefore the Rudra-lords are pictured as surrounding the Brahma egg densely, like bees covering blossoms.
uncertainties: The exact botanical image of kadamba and kesara-jāla is compressed into a single simile.
items.plain_english: The remaining Rudra-lords are Shighra, Nidhisha, Vidyesha, Shambhu, and Virabhadra; they surround the Brahma egg like bees covering honey and clusters of kadamba filaments.

items.question: How are the Shiva-Rudras arranged around the Brahma egg?
premises: The simile of bees is applied to the Shiva-Rudras.
They surround the Brahma egg with countless retinues.
Their arrangement is given in large numerical terms.
items.inference: Therefore the Shiva-Rudras form a vast, densely populated arrangement around the Brahma egg.
uncertainties: The exact arithmetic relation between śarāṣṭaniyutaṃ and koṭi is compressed and may reflect a traditional count.
items.plain_english: In the same way, the Shiva-Rudras, with countless attendants, surround the Brahma egg; their arrangement is described in vast numbers, such as forty niyutas and a crore.

items.question: What role do these Rudras play under Shrikantha's authority?
premises: These Rudras are presided over by Shrikantha.
They perform creation and withdrawal.
They exercise lordship over the gods, according to the Raurava Vartika.
items.inference: Therefore, under Shrikantha, these Rudras function as cosmic lords who create, withdraw, and rule the gods.
uncertainties: The exact scope of 'gods' here is not specified beyond the citation.
items.plain_english: Presided over by Shrikantha, these Rudras create and withdraw, and they hold lordship over the gods, as stated in the Raurava Vartika.

items.question: What alternative cosmological account is given in the Siddha Tantra?
premises: The Siddha Tantra gives a different account.
Beyond a hundred crores from the golden egg there are a hundred eggs.
These eggs increase in sequence and are associated with silver and other materials.
items.inference: Therefore the Siddha Tantra describes a further series of a hundred eggs arranged in an expanding sequence beyond the golden egg.
uncertainties: dvidviguṇaṃ is terse; it likely indicates successive doubling but the exact progression is compressed.
items.plain_english: But in the Siddha Tantra, beyond a hundred crores from the golden egg, there is a sequence of a hundred more eggs, successively doubled and associated with silver and other substances.

items.question: What happens within those successive eggs and what comes after them?
premises: In those eggs there are Brahmas in sequence.
Their lifespans are doubled in sequence.
They perish in order, and beyond their end another principle appears.
items.inference: Therefore the series of eggs contains successive Brahmas of increasing lifespan, culminating in a higher principle beyond them.
uncertainties: tattvamammayam is ambiguous in isolation; it clearly marks a higher tattva but its exact name is not explicit here.
items.plain_english: In those eggs, Brahmas exist in sequence with doubled lifespans; they perish in order, and at the end of that series a higher principle is reached.

items.question: How do the principles expand in scale from earth upward?
premises: From earth upward come water and the other principles in sequence.
Up to ego the expansion is tenfold.
Beyond that, intellect is a hundredfold.
items.inference: Therefore the tattvas are arranged in an ascending sequence with increasing orders of magnitude.
uncertainties: The verse gives ratios of expansion but does not specify the exact unit being multiplied.
items.plain_english: From earth upward come water and the rest in order; up to ego the scale increases tenfold, and beyond that intellect increases a hundredfold.

items.question: What magnitudes are assigned to the principles above intellect?
premises: Manifest nature is a thousandfold.
The masculine principle is ten thousandfold.
Niyati is a hundred thousandfold and leads to a millionfold beyond it.
items.inference: Therefore the higher principles continue the ascending scale through increasingly vast magnitudes.
uncertainties: The final phrase points forward to the next verse for the principle that is a millionfold.
items.plain_english: Above intellect, manifest nature is a thousandfold, purusha is ten thousandfold, and niyati is a hundred thousandfold, leading to a millionfold beyond it.

items.question: How do the magnitudes continue from kala up to the level beyond Ishvara?
premises: Up to kala the measure is ten millionfold.
Maya is a hundred millionfold.
Ishvara is a billionfold and leads to a thousand-crore-fold beyond.
items.inference: Therefore the cosmological scale continues to expand dramatically through kala, maya, and Ishvara.
uncertainties: The large number terms follow traditional usage; exact modern equivalents are approximate.
items.plain_english: Up to kala the scale is ten millionfold, Maya is a hundred millionfold, Ishvara is a billionfold, and beyond that it reaches a thousand crores.

items.question: What is the pervading reach of Sadakhya and its associated power?
premises: Sadakhya pervades at the vast scale indicated before.
It is accompanied by a multitude of powers.
The pervading goddess is established as pervading the entire path.
items.inference: Therefore Sadakhya, together with its powers, extends through the whole path as an all-pervading level.
uncertainties: The verse shifts between Sadakhya and the goddess; the doctrinal identity is implied rather than fully explained.
items.plain_english: Sadakhya pervades at that vast scale, and together with its multitude of powers the all-pervading goddess is established as pervading the entire path.

items.question: What is the status of Shiva-tattva relative to the rest of the path?
premises: Beyond the preceding levels is the pure, supreme Shiva principle.
That principle is immeasurable.
From water onward up to Shiva-tattva, none but Shiva has seen it.
items.inference: Therefore Shiva-tattva transcends the measurable path and is known directly only by Shiva.
uncertainties: The scope of 'seen' may include both direct vision and full knowledge.
items.plain_english: Beyond all that is the pure, supreme, immeasurable Shiva principle; from water up to Shiva-tattva, no one but Shiva has truly seen it.

items.question: Why is knowledge of Shiva said to be the supreme cause of liberation?
premises: Only Shiva fully knows the highest principle.
Therefore knowledge of Shiva is supreme.
Mahadeva states this in the Svacchanda scripture.
items.inference: Therefore supreme knowledge of Shiva is the true cause of liberation, as confirmed by scripture.
uncertainties: The verse functions as a bridge to the quoted authority in the next verse.
items.plain_english: For that reason, knowledge of Shiva is the supreme cause of liberation, as Mahadeva declares in the revered Svacchanda scripture.

rows.grounds: names the subject and rejected means

items.question: Can a bound soul attain liberation without Shiva-knowledge and Shaiva initiation?
premises: A bound soul does not attain liberation by hundreds of other knowledges.
Knowledge of Shiva does not arise without Shaiva initiation.
Liberation depends on that knowledge.
items.inference: Therefore liberation requires Shaiva initiation and the arising of knowledge of Shiva.
uncertainties: The verse is presented as scriptural authority; its doctrinal force is clear though the citation is indirect here.
items.plain_english: A bound soul does not attain liberation by hundreds of other kinds of knowledge; knowledge of Shiva does not arise without receiving Shaiva initiation.
